name: TODAY feedback ON
description: Runnable right now: all 18 headline cells pass the density gate on the corpus as it stands (backfilled through 2025-03 + 2025-11..2026-06, relevance-screened).
notes: STALENESS IS FIXED. The original problem was decisions made past the end of the
news corpus (it stopped 2025-11-12; 15.3% of legacy decisions fell after it).
The corpus now runs to 2026-06-30 and every window's last decision lands before
that, so ZERO decisions in this grid are stale.
GATE = 45 screened articles per 180 days, measured on each cell's THINNEST
decision. Chosen from the data, not by feel: on today's screened corpus the
worst cell sees 47 in 180 days, so 45 clears all 18 cells with a small margin.
WHY 180 DAYS AND NOT 90: at 90 days the 12x cadence bottoms out at 12 screened
articles for every window, because the 2025-04..2025-09 stretch is not backfilled
yet. A 180-day window is also the more defensible definition of 'recent' for a
12-month buy-and-hold strategy reading a 2-year lookback. State this in the paper
as a pre-registered density criterion, and use the SAME numbers for the OFF arm.
REMAINING LIMITATION TO DISCLOSE: 2025-04..2025-09 is still thinner than the rest
of the corpus. The gate keeps every cell above a stated floor, but density is not
uniform across windows. Re-run with a higher gate once that backfill completes.
order_mode=weights removes the 52% budget-violation rate but makes these runs
NOT comparable to the legacy 90 (which used dollar orders). That is intended.
dry_run is TRUE. Untick 'Dry-run (no API)' in the GUI to actually spend budget.
